context_pill: Capital Gains - Cost of Acquisition of Inherited Property
example_summary: Abraham inherited a property purchased by Xavier on 26.05.2002 for ₹ 5,00,000, cleared a mortgage of ₹ 15,00,000 on 12.02.2010, and sold it for ₹ 55,00,000 on 16.04.2025. Taxable LTCG for A.Y. 2026-27 is ₹ 35,00,000.
source_provision:
| Statutory Provision | Applicability / Trigger Event | Legal Consequence & Tax Treatment |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 49(1)(iiia)** | Property acquired under a Will or inheritance | Cost of acquisition shall be deemed to be the cost for which the previous owner acquired the property. |
| **Section 48 & Section 55(2)** | Expenditure incurred for clearing a mortgage on inherited property | Amount paid by the successor to clear outstanding mortgage debt to obtain a clear title is added to the cost of acquisition. |


> [!IMPORTANT]
> Judicial Precedent: The Supreme Court in **RM. Arunachalam v. CIT [1997] 227 ITR 222** established that payment of an outstanding mortgage debt by a successor to secure absolute ownership and clear title constitutes an allowable cost of acquisition.


> [!WARNING]
> Statutory Trap: Do not index the predecessor's cost from the year of inheritance; indexation must be calculated starting from the Financial Year in which the asset was first held by the assessee or previous owner as per statutory indexing rules.

director.justification: Computes Abraham's taxable long-term capital gain from selling inherited property by ledgering cost to previous owner under Section 49(1)(iiia) and mortgage clearance cost per RM. Arunachalam v. CIT.
director.visual_metaphor: A multi-layered financial balance ledger adding original purchase cost and mortgage discharge cost to deduct from total sale consideration.
